rows.grounds: from śrī (prosperity, fortune); expresses relation to prosperity in the sequence śriyo vidyā-puraścaryā-phalaṃ
vidyā (knowledge, learning; in tantric context may denote mantra-knowledge); first member in vidyā-puraścaryā
puraścaryā (preliminary or preparatory ritual observance); paired with vidyā as vidyā-puraścaryā
phala (fruit, result); denotes the outcome of the preceding vidyā-puraścaryā
sāṅga (with limbs/auxiliary parts); qualifies the observance as complete with its components
dina (day); first element of repeated dine dine indicating daily recurrence
dina (day); repeated after preceding dine to express day-by-day continuity
